output.answer: At the before air, the nearest solid-fuel runs recorded flames near the same pressure; at the after air, runs at the stated air include flames as well as some recorded extinguishments, so lowering oxygen alone is not supported as a reliable fire response. The nearest after-air result runs are different fuels and investigations, and do not show that this cabin fire will go out.
output.whatChanges: No run sits exactly at the before air: the closest result runs were 8.3–8.4 oxygen points away and 0.1 psi away, and recorded flames for SIBAL and PMMA [bass-asrun-55] [bass-asrun-60]; two nearby PMMA runs recorded extinguishment, with the outcome read from notes [bass-asrun-61] [bass-asrun-62]. At the after air, 133 runs are at that air; among the examples, a flame was recorded as extinguished when airflow was reduced or stopped [bass-asrun-92] [bass-asrun-29], while the closest stated-result runs at the exact oxygen and pressure recorded extinguishment for other fuels, with the outcome based on notes [bass-ii-p22b]. The app’s estimate changes from “Likely to burn” (93%, 90% range 79–100%, high confidence) before to “Likely to burn” (96%, 90% range 93–99%, high confidence) after; both are estimates, not test results.
output.whatYouWouldSee: At the lower air, notes describe flames becoming blue and dim before extinguishing when airflow was turned off [bass-asrun-30] [bass-asrun-28]; another run notes soot during flow and a blue flame at very low flow [bass-asrun-92]. Less oxygen can weaken a flame, but these observations do not establish that lowering cabin oxygen alone will extinguish this fire.

output.instead: The evidence points more directly to controlling ventilation: several notes-based BASS runs report extinguishment when airflow was turned down or off, including [bass-asrun-29] and [bass-asrun-30]; this is not a guarantee for this fire. Since runs are available at the after air, no single missing-condition test can settle the question; a same-fuel, same-pressure test at the after air with controlled oxygen and airflow changes would be the useful comparison.
